$comment: The single definition of every version we track upstream. A Dockerfile ARG, a seam manifest, a peerDependency and a release manifest that each carried their own copy meant 'bump the pin' was four edits and one of them was always missed. Tests assert every derived copy equals the value here; the nightly compatibility matrix is one job that loops over these keys.

dsh.notes: The 0.1.5 line's second release candidate, and the newest thing npm holds. Adopted on the criterion in decision #25 -- probed against the running binary of this version plus our own battery -- not on the tag; at adoption the dist-tags were latest=0.1.5-rc.1, next=0.1.5-rc.2, alpha=0.1.5-alpha.2, and the GitHub tag was 0.1.5-rc.2. rc.2 rather than the `latest` tag, because rc.1 is not a version that can be pinned: its own 61 subpackage ranges read `^0.1.5-rc.1`, npm resolves a prerelease caret to the highest in range, and installing rc.1 therefore lays down a tree of rc.2 subpackages (measured: 230 of them, with rc.1 present only as the root). The two published closures differ in exactly one file of 3406, `dsh/package.json`. Measured before adopting: 224 -> 241 `@deepseek-ai/*` packages, 19 added, 2 removed (node-addon-landlock-run* gave way to node-addon-system*, a different sandbox backend), and 214 of the 224 carried over changed content -- this is a real upgrade across three releases, not a retag like 0.1.2-alpha.5 -> rc.1 was. What survived: every seam name the manifest lists still appears in the shipped code (9 events, 18 session-event types, 6 turn-end kinds, 7+5 services, 5 mux frames, 26 packages), and `verify-harness-seams` fails on the same three things here as at 0.1.2-rc.1, so the upgrade added no seam debt. What moved: the RPC surface went 74 -> 84, and all ten new methods are denied (`workspaceFiles/*` reads any absolute path the runtime user can read -- upstream's own parameter documentation says "files outside it are allowed" -- `fileUploads/upload` writes bytes past the source ledger, `sessionFeedback/record` is `messageFeedback` renamed, `goals/get` was already covered). The composition was recorded live rather than described: 150 -> 157 rows, all 25 invariants we hold still hold, and the three upstream defaults that moved are all ones we override or do not use (`agent-default-model.model` deepseek-v4-flash -> deepseek-flash, the `tool-str-replace-editor` row gone, `system-prompt.config.persona` split into personaPrefix/personaSuffix). `DSH_PUBLISHED_BEFORE` in the runtime Dockerfile moves with this pin and is not a version string, so no sweep finds it; the value here was checked by installing through it and counting drift (231 dsh* packages, 0 drifted). Subpackage `latest` dist-tags mostly still point at 0.0.1-rc.1, so every install writes an exact version and the peer ranges are declared explicitly. `dsh plugin` manages a profile with pnpm and writes a pnpm-workspace.yaml listing the profile itself, which pnpm 9 refuses to add into without -w; this pin tracks DSH's own packageManager, not the workspace's. Upstream also tags prereleases on GitHub that npm never receives, so the matrix reports the GitHub tag as `upstreamTag` beside the npm `latest`: npm is what is installable and what `behind` means, the tag is the early warning.

openlist.notes: Self-hosted drive aggregator; v4.2.6 (2026-09-01), including access-control and authentication fixes from the current stable release. EviMed uses the pinned list, get and link contracts, then reads bytes through OpenList's same-origin proxy without following a provider-controlled redirect. The service runs with an isolated data volume and tenant-prefixed paths.

mineru.notes: Document parsing for CJK layout, tables and formulas; PyPI 3.4.5. `pypdf` stays as the fast plain-text fallback.

openviking.notes: The one recall index of the base stack: it ranks both the research-memory records and the capsule facts, whose authoritative rows stay in the control-plane PostgreSQL. Never a record store — its `write` offers replace/append/create and no compare-and-swap, so the `expectedVersion` the record store enforces has no equivalent and two concurrent edits of one record would silently lose one. `embedding` is what `scripts/ops/configure-production-state.mjs` renders into the server's ov.conf (provider `dashscope` with `input: "text"`, which appends `/compatible-mode/v1` to `apiBase` itself and is the only provider that sends `dimensions`); changing the model or the dimension invalidates every stored vector, so it takes a `pnpm rebuild:memory-index --all`. `rerank` is read by the control plane, not by the server: `/search/find` never reranks and `/search/search`, which does, navigates by directory abstracts no VLM generates here and returns nothing for this layout, so the reranker runs where the hydrated text already is and the ov.conf carries no rerank section. Both model ids were probed live on 2026-09-14 with a real key: `qwen3.7-text-embedding` answers at dimension 1024 with and without an explicit `dimensions` parameter, and `qwen3-rerank` answers on both the OpenAI-compatible reranks path pinned here and the native one, with identical scores. A server rendered from these values started healthy as uid 10001 and embedded 300 records; recall@5 over the twelve eval questions went 0.667 (term matcher) to 0.933 (this embedder) to 1.000 (with the rerank), which is what `evals/memory-recall/README.md` records. The server is AGPL-3.0 and runs unmodified as its own service; the CLI, plugins and examples are Apache-2.0. The container tag carries a `v` prefix (`ghcr.io/volcengine/openviking:v0.4.19`) while the PyPI version does not; the unprefixed tag simply does not exist and a compose file that names it fails at pull. Releases land every few days and have moved data layouts before (0.3.x needed a staged migration through 0.4.5; 0.4.18 changed ACL fields from boolean to string), so the pin moves only through the matrix. `@openviking/dsh-memory-plugin` is listed for the local `evimed-web` profile only: it spawns an MCP proxy that talks to the server directly, which the hosted runtime may not do.
